$Comment: The introduction to the sawmill: the Adventurer's Guide, standing in the Forgotten Temple,
points the player at the sawyer working a few paces away across the same landing. The quest
exists to make the player look up and notice him.
Npc.ViewId names the guide's temple id, so the guide is who OFFERS it: it appears on their
quest list down in the temple, right after the meeting that brought the player there. The step
names the sawyer's role id instead, so the errand is taken from one character and discharged at
another. His placement authors no Identity.NpcId, so the character IS the role, and any other
standing of Mmo_Sawyer credits the step just as well.
TurnInAt names the sawyer, so the reward is collected where the errand ends rather than on a
walk back to the guide: the quest sits in the Claim bucket and waits in the log until the
player collects it from the sawyer's own quest list. Point TurnInAt somewhere else and the
reward follows; leave it out and the quest may be collected anywhere, which also puts it on
every other character's list.
CompletionDialogue names the sawyer's own conversation, so collecting the reward at him plays
his next line instead of leaving the player looking at the quest list. His conversation picks
its own opening screen from there, and with this introduction settled the first job he can
offer is Timber Rights, so the player lands on the screen that hands it over. It only plays
when the player is actually standing at a character; collecting from the book out in the world
just pays. Point it at another conversation to change who answers, or leave it out and
collecting pays with nobody speaking.
A talk step is credited by a MarkTalked beat inside the conversation, never by pressing F, so
the sawyer's dialogue carries one on the line the player picks. Re-point the step and that beat
has to move with it.
The Woodcutting experience is deliberately small: it is a nod toward the skill the whole sawmill
chain trains, not a payout worth walking down for on its own. Edit Rewards to re-tune it.
Requires.Quests names a quest the mod jar ships, which is what chains this pack onto the end of
the starter run; without the jar's temple quest finished the guide simply has nothing to offer.
The feature factor keeps the quest out of the log on a server with the station engine switched
off, where the sawyer never appears at all.
Listing.Hidden keeps it off open listings until it is taken; a giver always lists its own
quests, so the guide still offers it in the temple.
